snippet_en: The editor-in-chief of the local newspaper, “Young Far Easterner”, was fined for the article “History with Gayography.” This article tells a story of an openly gay school geography teacher in Khabarovsk who was fired because of his sexual orientation. The court found that this article “promoted non-traditional sexual relations among minors”.
snippet_ru: Главный редактор газеты “Молодой Дальневосточник” был оштрафован за статью “История с гейографией.” В этой статье рассказывается история открыто гомосексуального учителя географии в школе в Хабаровске, который был уволен из-за своей сексуальной ориентации. Суд установил, что эта статья “пропагандировала нетрадиционные сексуальные отношения среди несовершеннолетних”.

snippet_en: The editor-in-chief of the Kursk online media outlet “CRNews” was fined for publishing the article "You and I won't make it" (09.08.2013), which, according to the court, “contained information aimed at developing non-traditional sexual attitudes in minors.” A judicial expert determined that the article contained “a sufficient number of suggestive techniques to [...] influence the psyche of children in terms of the presence of propaganda of homosexualism.” The expert classified phrases from the article as: “direct suggestive commands” ('Why don't you try becoming a lesbian'); “truismes” ('There aren't many joys in the life of gays'); “programming homosexual behavior” ('I can become a good mother'); “phrases appealing to presubposition” ('you know that gays earn more'); “use of manipulative figures of speech” (the expert wrote that the sentence 'After all, the male body with which God mistakenly endowed me is more resilient' “contains the false premise that God can make mistakes”); “analogous phrases with a false premise” ('Two dads? What a shame. But what about a mother, a grandmother, an aunt – is that a normal family?!'). The article is no longer available online.
An individual was fined for selling four children's T-shirts that “contained graphic information depicting the attractiveness of non-traditional sexual relations” in a clothing shop.

The director of the company “Kometa-Plus” was fined for distributing the board game “Forfeits”, which contained “elements promoting non-traditional sexual relations” among minors, as the mass media reported. The case was initiated after the organisation “Parental Committee of Stavropol” appealed to the prosecutor's office. The game asked the participants to roleplay different situations, such as “Pretend to be a same-sex couple on a date” and “Portray a man-loving Rambo” (text on the chips). The company that manufactured the board game was also fined (see case 7-149/2014).
snippet_ru: Директор компании “Комета-Плюс” была оштрафована за распространение настольной игры “Фанты”, которая, как сообщали СМИ, содержала “элементы, пропагандирующие нетрадиционные сексуальные отношения” среди несовершеннолетних. Дело было возбуждено после обращения в прокуратуру организации “Родительский комитет Ставрополья”. Игра предлагала разыгрывать различные ситуации, такие как “Изобразите свидание однополой пары” или “Изобразите любящего мужчин Рэмбо” (текст на фишках). Компания-производитель настольной игры также была оштрафована (см. дело 7-149/2014).

snippet_en: “Kometa-Plus”, the manufacturer of the board game “Forfeits”, was fined for “dissemination of information aimed at developing non-traditional sexual attitudes in minors”, according to the court. As the judicial expertise stated, “individual elements of the game [...] directly and indirectly promote homosexuality”. The game asked the players to roleplay different situations, such as “Pretend to be a same-sex couple on a date” and “Portray a man-loving Rambo” (text on the chips). Earlier, the general director of the company was also fined for distributing the same board game (see case 12-28/2014).
snippet_ru: “Комета-Плюс”, компания-производитель настольной игры “Фанты”, была оштрафована за “распространение информации, направленной на формирование у несовершеннолетних нетрадиционных сексуальных установок”, согласно суду. Как заключила судебная экспертиза, “отдельные элементы игры [...] непосредственным и опосредованным способом пропагандируют гомосексуализм”. Игра предлагала разыгрывать различные ситуации, такие как “Изобразите свидание однополой пары” или “Изобразите любящего мужчин Рэмбо” (текст на фишках). Директор этой комании также была оштрафована за эту игру (см. дело 12-28/2014).

snippet_en: An activist was fined for his single protest, during which he displayed a banner with the text “Being gay and loving gays is normal, beating gays and killing gays is a crime”. The activist appealed his fine twice, but the Supreme Court of the Republic of Tatarstan still deemed the poster to promote non-traditional sexual relations.

A magazine published the article entitled “When like charges attract” about lesbian relationships, which authorities classified as material presenting same-sex relationships positively to minors and therefore treated as unlawful for public distribution.

The editor-in-chief of the newspaper “Tvoi den'” was fined for publishing the article “I don't consider sex with a girlfriend to be cheating on my husband”, discussing romantic and sexual relationships between women, which authorities classified as inappropriate for distribution to minors and treated as unlawful promotion of same-sex relationships.
snippet_ru: Газета “Твой день” опубликовала статью “Секс с подружкой я не считаю изменой мужу” (номер 143), в которой обсуждались романтические и сексуальные отношения между женщинами, которые власти квалифицировали как неподходящие для распространения среди несовершеннолетних и расценили как незаконную пропаганду однополых отношений.

snippet_en: An individual was fined for administering a social media group “Kids against homophobia” in VKontakte, where he posted such messages as “Love each other…”, “Love conquers all…”, and “It’s nicest to fall asleep hugging your loved one…”, attaching photos of two hugging teenagers, two sleeping teenagers, and two kissing teenagers. The court viewed these posts to be “portraying same-sex relationships as emotionally and aesthetically appealing to minors”.

The journalist Elena Klimova created the online support project “Children-404. LGBT-teenagers”, which included groups on social media, in which queer teens shared their experiences and sought support. The project regularly published their letters. The court determined that the project’s content constituted unlawful promotion of same-sex relationships among minors. In 2025, the European Court of Human Rights ruled that the decision of the Russian court violates the Articles 8 and 10 of the ECHR.

A foreign national was fined and ordered to leave the country for using social media to message with a minor in a way authorities interpreted as “promoting non-traditional sexual relationships”. The court decision did not specify which messages or actions constituted the violation.
The LGBT-support organisation, Maximum, which provided legal and psychological assistance, was fined for publishing its content online.
A publishing house was fined for the online article “Plan B. A Lesbian Sex Masterclass” in Maxim magazine.
snippet_ru: Издательство оштрафовано за онлайн-статью “План Би. Мастер-класс по сексу от лесбиянок” в журнале Maxim.

snippet_en: A school teacher was prosecuted for images, quotes, and discussions related to same-sex relationships on her social media pages.
An individual was fined for posting images on his VKontakte social media page, which the court found to be “promoting non-traditional sexual relationships”. What the images depicted is unknown.

An activist was prosecuted for reposting English-language mass media articles on her social media and publishing posts about the organisation “The Youth Coalition for Sexual and Reproductive Rights”. The authorities translated the articles into Russian using an online translation tool and concluded that they promoted “non-traditional sexual relations” among minors. The articles were “Ireland becomes first country to legalise gay marriage by popular vote” by The Guardian and “Russian LGBT Activists March In 'Rainbow May Day'” by BuzzFeed.

A VKontakte user was fined for uploading photos of men with “well-developed muscles up to the waist” onto his page. According to the court, these images and text accompanying them promoted “non-traditional sexual relationships” among minors.
A single protester was fined for “speaking slogans about freedom of non-traditional sexual relations”, while holding an “LGBT flag” and a banner near a school entrance.

An activist held a single protest in the city centre, holding a banner that read, “Look at me. #TDOV — Transgender Day of Visibility.” In addition to the banner, the court recognised another “evidence” of the “promotion of the non-traditional sexual relations among minors”, which was rainbow-coloured knee socks the activist wore during the protest.

An admin of a VKontakte page about gay dating was fined for “propaganda among minors of non-traditional sexual relations”. According to the mass media, the individual administered the VK page until 2010, and the content was posted to the page by its members. Other details of the case are unknown; the court did not publish the decision.

A moderator of a VKontakte page was fined, becasue the page “contained text, images, audio, and video […] prohibited for distribution among children, namely, information aimed at denying traditional spiritual, moral, and family values and promoting non-traditional sexual relations”, according to the court. The judicial expertise concluded: “the main theme of this webpage is the recognition of the normality and equivalence of sexual relations between a man and a man, in connection with which indirect signs of distorted ideas about the social equivalence of traditional and non-traditional sexual relations are present.” In court, the defendant explained that this VK page was about dating among homosexual people. The exact content that constituted the violation is unknown.

The organiser of the “Spirit of Fire” film festival was fined for the textual description of the Russian film “Outlaw” (Ksenia Ratushnaya, 2020) on the festival website that read “A gay high school student and a young criminal are trying to win back the most popular guy in the school. An army general and a transgender dancer in 1985 put career and life on the line to be together.”

Yuliya Tsvetkova, an artist and activist from Komsomolsk-on-Amur, was fined for two social media posts expressing support for young subscribers of the VKontakte group “The Last Supper – LGBTQIAP+on-Amur” accompanied by images of cartoon cats coloured in queer flags. Yulia appealed the court decision twice, but the cassation court upheld the punishment.

Anastasia Panchenko, an activist and coordinator of Alexey Navalny's (a politician, Putin's ctitic) Krasnodar office, was fined for two Instagram photos of kissing couples that, according to the court, were “aimed at instilling non-traditional sexual attitudes in minors.” In one photo, a person is holding the banner “Love is stronger than fear”.

A VKontakte user was fined for posting “We invite you to sign up for Irkutsk LGBT Chat group. We're looking for active kids. Ages 14+ [...]”, which the court found to be “promotion of non-traditional sexual relations” among minors.

The music channel “Muz‑TV” was fined after its 2021 awards show broadcast featured celebrities who, according to the court, “did not correspond to the image of a man of a traditional sexual orientation.” The court mentioned Filipp Kirkorov and Dava surrounded by shirtless men, Alexey Zhidkovsky “demonstrating traditional feminine characteristics”, and another person [Igor Sinyak] “in a women's evening dress with a train.”

The editor-in-chief of the online mass media “7×7 — Horizontal Russia” was fined for six publications from 2021. Based on the “psycho-linguistic” expert analysis, the court deemed the publications to be “promoting non-traditional sexual relationships”. It is unclear what exactly constituted the violation. The titles of the publications were redacted in the court decision. Based on the indicated time of the publications, we identified one of them, titled “‘This is some kind of cave-like savagery.’ An unidentified individual attacked LGBT activists with a spray can in the city centre of Yaroslavl” from 12.06.2021.

Journalist Yuri Dud was fined for his interview with an artist, Fedor Pavlov-Andreevich, who spoke about homophobia in Russia during the interview. The court found that this interview “with an open homosexualist and activist who emigrated from Russia” promoted “non-traditional sexual relations among minors.”

A school principal was fined for a banner dedicated to International Tolerance Day placed in the school hallway. The photo of this banner was published on Telegram, which led to an investigation. One of the pieces of evidence the court admitted was a “comprehensive psycho-cultural examination”, which found the banner made by students to contain “symbols of LGBD-community” and “signs of promotion of non-traditional sexual relations among minors.”

The online marketplace “Wildberries” was fined for several items “promoting non-traditional sexual relationships”: “2018 Calendar. Erotica-2”, the book “First Orgasm in My Life. From the ‘Diary of a Latent Lesbian’ series” by Olga Serebryanskaya, “30x40 painting on canvas on a wooden stretcher”, and “Flag/Rainbow Flag/Non-traditional Flag 90x150”. The court concluded that these items were “aimed at developing non-traditional sexual attitudes in minors” because they were sold without age restriction.

A foreign national was fined and ordered to leave the country for posting a profile on a website for trans women escorts. According to the police protocol, the creator of the profile, “being a male, writes about himself in the feminine gender [...] publicly expressing his interest in the attractiveness of non-traditional relationships” by posting “information about the cost of intimate services, personal physiological data, and terms of service provision.”

A foreign national was fined and ordered to leave the country for posting a profile on a website for trans women escorts. The court decision stated that the profile was “aimed at developing non-traditional sexual relations” because its creator, “being a male, writes about himself in the feminine gender”, and “posts photos in a female guise with exposed female breasts and male genitalia (penis), with dark long hair and makeup.”

A foreign national was detained and ordered to leave the country for posting a profile on the social media website “Drug Vokrug”. According to the court, the profile owner “being a male, posts photos of himself in a women's dress and a long-haired wig, and refers to himself in the feminine gender”, suggesting “intimate services for non-traditional relations”.

A foreign national was fined and ordered to leave the country for posting a profile on the trans women escort website. The court decision states that the profile was “aimed at developing non-traditional sexual relations” because its creator, “being a male, posts photos of himself in female guise, specifically in women's clothing (a skirt), with signs of female breasts, with long blond hair, makeup, and with exposed male genitalia (penis).”

A German citizen was fined and ordered to leave the country for corresponding with a man on the gay dating app “Hornet”. The court found that the defendant's private messages “promoted non-traditional sexual attitudes, the attractiveness of non-traditional sexual relations, and a distorted idea of the social equivalence of traditional and non-traditional sexual relations”, and that the defendant “exerted ideological and psychological influence on [the message recipient], which led to the imposition of a system of ideas and values alien and destructive to Russian society.” The judge cited three messages the defendant sent to another “Hornet” user: “Being gay is allowed”; “It is simply sad that we have to separate people depending on what they do in bed… this should be a private matter”; “In the West, they are all so absorbed in themselves that they do not actually give their partner emotions and passion in bed.” The user with whom the defendant corresponded was a witness in this case, stating in his testimony that he responded to the defendant that “in Russia, LGBT is prohibited both morally and legally.”

snippet_en: The creator of the YouTube channel “HAOYANG & GELA”, a Chinese national, was detained and then ordered to leave the country after the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Kazan established that 19 videos he uploaded “depicted non-traditional sexual relations.” The court described the videos showing two individuals “being male, they kiss each other, hug, touch each other on various parts of the body, including the genital area.” There are also several video titles mentioned in the case, such as “How do gay couples sleep? Kiss me all night long”, “We're back, a love story in the land of hate”, “Watch us recreate kissing scenes”, “I want to hold you while I sleep”, “Who knows me better, my boyfriend or my best friend?”, “Our first time, candid stories”, “Our favourite positions during...”, “25 Types of kissing with my boyfriend”. It is said that the police also “established that out of 64.9K subscribers [of the YouTube channel], 1,791 were minors”, so the judge argued that the videos promoted “non-traditional sexual relations” and “desire to change sex” among minors.
snippet_ru: Создатель YouTube-канала «HAOYANG & GELA», гражданин Китая, был арестован на семь суток и затем выдворен из России после того, как МВД в Казани нашло 19 размещённых им видеороликов с “изображением нетрадиционных сексуальных отношений”. В судебном постановлении описываются видео, в которых пара, “будучи представителями мужского пола, они целуются друг с другом, обнимаются, трогают друг друга за различные части тела, в том числе в районе половых органов”. Суд также упомянул видеоролики с такими названиями: “Как спит гей пара? Целуй меня всю ночь”, “Мы вернулись, история любви в стране ненависти”, “Смотрите, как мы воссоздаем сцены поцелуев”, “Я хочу обнимать тебя во время сна”, “Кто знает меня лучше мой парень или лучший друг?”, “Наш первый раз, откровенные истории”, “Наши любимые позы во время..”, “25 видов поцелуев с моим парнем”. Согласно материалам дела, полиция установила, “что из 64,9 тысяч подписчиков [YouTube-канала] 1791 человек являются несовершеннолетними”, в связи с чем суд пришёл к выводу, что видеоролики пропагандировали среди несовершеннолетних “нетрадиционные сексуальные отношения” и были способны вызвать “желание сменить пол”.

snippet_en: An individual was fined for posting on a Telegram channel. The court stated that the user “being male, repeatedly posted photos and videos of himself in women's clothing and makeup, and videos of himself engaging in non-traditional sexual acts with another male”, which constituted the “promotion of non-traditional sexual relations and preferences or sex change.”

A Saint Petersburg company was fined for online advertisements in VKontakte. One ad was about the nightclub “Born”, “aimed primarily at recreation for people of non-traditional sexual orientation”, according to the court case. Another ad mentioned the gay sauna “Near the Circus”. One piece of evidence in the case was a report to the police by a man who saw the club's advertisement online and decided to visit. As he stated, he saw some rooms in the club that “shocked” him.

The online streaming service “Tricolor Kino i TV Online” was fined for showing the film “Blow Dry” (2001, Paddy Breathnach) labelled “16+” with a 10-second scene (01:21:47-01:21:57) of “two same-sex characters (female) kissing in a sexual context”, which the court found to be the “demonstration of non-traditional sexual relationships to minors.”

A Ukrainian citizen was found guilty of “promoting non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences or sex change” via the internet. The court did not specify the exact content that constituted the violation. As the judge reasoned, because the defendant was registered in one of the occupied Ukrainian regions, “he cannot be subject to deportation outside the Russian Federation”, so the defendant was arrested.

A Kyrgyzstan citizen was arrested for 24 hours and sentenced to an administrative expulsion for “promoting non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences or sex change” via the internet.  The court did not specify the exact content that constituted the violation.

Yan Dvorkin, head of the support centre for transgender and non-binary people, “Center-T”, was fined for a Telegram post announcing a marriage with such phrases as “So, gay marriages are here to stay!” and “Our insidious plan to legalise same-sex marriage was successful.” The court found Yan's post to be “promoting non-traditional sexual relationships” because the judicial expertise concluded that it presented relationships “not between a man and a woman” in a positive light and characterised such relationships as “natural”. The picture is a screenshot of the post mentioned in the court order.

The website editor of the streaming service “Tricolor Kino i TV Online” was fined for the film “Blow Dry” (2001, Paddy Breathnach) labelled “16+” with a 10-second scene (01:21:47-01:21:57) of “two same-sex characters (female) kissing in a sexual context”, which the court found to be “demonstrating non-traditional sexual relationships to minors.” The legal entity which owns the streaming service was also fined for the same film scene (case 5-493/23).

snippet_en: The company “DotDTechnology”, which owns the TV channel “Clubbing TV”, was issued a warning for airing six music videos: “Muchas” by Myd feat. Cola Boyy (2018), “Smile” by Galantis (2013), “Ride It” by Regard (2019), “La Lueur” by Holism (2022), “Hold Me To The Light” by KAS:ST (2021), and “You Boy” by Arigato Massaï feat. Yanis (2020). According to the court, these videos “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relationships and preferences to minors” because they were labelled “16+”. The judge decided to replace a fine with a warning because it was the company's first-time administrative offence. However, later, the company was fined by the same court for airing other music videos (see case 05-0475/2023).

The legal entity “Inetra”, which owned the streaming service “Peers.TV”, was fined for “demonstration of materials containing LGBT scenes to minors”, according to mass media. The exact content that constituted the violation is unknown. An administrative protocol against the company was drawn up by Roskomnadzor, the Russian mass media regulator.

The streaming service “PREMIER” was fined for the films “Perfect Strangers” (Paolo Genovese, 2016) and “Blow Dry” (2001, Paddy Breathnach). According to the court, these films “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences” among minors, because they were labelled “16+”. Roskomnadzor, the Russian mass media regulator, identified eight scenes in the first film (00:58:46–00:59:09, 01:01:05–01:01:35, 01:01:36–01:03:50, 01:04:32–01:04:55, 01:05:56–01:06:35, 01:17:24–01:17:29, 01:17:40–01:20:40, 01:22:10–01:22:21) “demonstrating (or describing) homosexual relations between men, as well as references to homosexual relationships.” In the film “Blow Dry”, Roskomnadzor found the scene (01:21:45-01:22:01) with “two characters of the same sex (female) kissing in a sexual context.”

The editor-in-chief of “Clubbing TV” was fined for airing several music videos labelled “16+.” According to Roskomnadzor, the Russian mass media regulator, these videos “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relations and (or) preferences, including descriptions, depictions of non-traditional sexual relations and (or) preferences, or capable of causing a desire in minors to change sex, using mass media.” The court did not specify which videos or scenes violated the law.

The film distribution company “Russian Report” was fined for airing the TV series “Made in Italy” (Camilla Nesbitt, 2019) on the “KinoLiving” TV channel with the label “16+”. Roskomnadzor, the Russian mass media regulator, found that the fifth episode of the TV series “contained information (visual) consistent with the signs of demonstrating non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences, [...] conveyed through verbal and visual components: the address ‘honey’ [...] and displyas of a kiss and hug”, which, according to the court, is prohibited to distribute among minors.

The streaming platform “Start.ru” was fined for distributing “Perfect Strangers” (2016, Paolo Genovese). The court held that the film contained depictions and verbal references to same-sex relations between men, including scenes in which one character’s male partner sends intimate messages and the group discusses his sexual orientation. As stated in the ruling, the platform had allowed minors to access content containing “scenes demonstrating (describing) homosexual relations between men, as well as references to homosexual relations,” including dialogue such as: “If my best friend is gay, I want to know it … then I will decide myself how to relate to it.” The scenes identified by the court: 00:58:46–00:59:09 — The court highlighted a phone conversation in which a male caller confronts another male character about emotional intimacy, interpreting it as an explicit reference to same-sex desire: “Why did you leave? … You still cannot decide who you like: men or women.”; 01:01:36–01:03:50 — The ruling focused on a group discussion where friends react to the presumed homosexuality of one of the men, including statements about disclosure, friendship, and social acceptance: “If my best friend is gay, I want to know it … then I will decide myself how to relate to it.”; 01:17:40–01:20:40 — The court separately analysed the later confession scene in which one character openly identifies himself as gay and reflects on fear of disclosure: “The truth is, the faggot is me … How could I even tell you that I am gay?”

The legal entity which owns the streaming service “Megafon TV” was fined for the films “Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason” (Beeban Kidron, 2004), “Blow Dry” (2001, Paddy Breathnach), “Three Many Weddings” (Javier Ruiz Caldera, 2013), and “Greed” (Michael Winterbottom, 2019). According to the court, these films “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences” among minors, because they were labelled “16+”. It is not specified what scenes exactly constituted the violation.

The streaming service “Kinopoisk” was fined for distributing ten films: “Perfect Strangers” (Paolo Genovese, 2016), “Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason” (Beeban Kidron, 2004), “Three Many Weddings” (Javier Ruiz Caldera, 2013), “Easy A” (Will Gluck, 2010), “Blow Dry” (Paddy Breathnach, 2001), “Compartment No. 6” (Juho Kuosmanen, 2021), “Greed” (Michael Winterbottom, 2019), “Green Book” (Peter Farrelly, 2018), “The Amusement Park” (the title translated from Russian, the exact film is unknown), and “Beanpole” (Kantemir Balagov, 2019). According to the court, these films “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences to minors” and should have been marked “18+” instead of “16+”. The court did not specify the exact scenes in these movies that constituted the violation.

The editor-in-chief of the TV channel “TV-3 Russia” was fined for airing the film “Piranha 3D” (Alexandre Aja, 2010) twice with the label “16+”. Roskomnadzor, the Russian mass media regulator, identified two scenes in the film “demonstrating non-traditional sexual relations” among minors: “a girl licking salt off another girl’s body and a prolonged kiss expressing sexual passion (timestamps 00:51:10–00:51:28 and 00:55:21–00:55:39).”

The company that owns the streaming service “Ivi” was fined for the film “Perfect Strangers” (Paolo Genovese, 2016), labelled “16+”, because it “demonstrated non-traditional sexual relations and/or preferences.” It is not specified which scenes exactly constituted the violation.

The legal entity “FONBET TV”, which owns the music TV channel “TNT Music”, was fined for airing the music video “Summer Really Hurt Us” (2022) by ALMA, labelled “16+”. According to the court, the video contained “information depicting non-traditional sexual relationships and/or preferences that is prohibited for distribution to children.” The scene that violated the law was “an image of two individuals of the same biological sex (female) kissing.”

The TV channel “Eurokino” was fined for broadcasting “French Women” (2014, Audrey Dana). The court found that the film contained material classified as “demonstrating non-traditional sexual relations and preferences”. According to the ruling, the broadcaster had committed “the dissemination among minors of information demonstrating non-traditional sexual relations and (or) preferences, including description and depiction of non-traditional sexual relations and (or) preferences.” The amount of the fine has been redacted from the court ruling.

The company “ER–Telecom Holding”, which owns the streaming service “Movix”, was fined for distributing the films “Perfect Strangers” (Paolo Genovese, 2016) and “Loud Connection” (Alexey Nuzhnyy, 2019), labelled “16+”. snippet_en: An individual who attended a drag performance at a Halloween party in the nightclub “Dark Horse” in Yaroslavl  was fined after the police raided the club. The details of this case are unknown; the court did not publish the decision. The defendant appealed, but the decision was upheld by the Leninsky District Court of Yaroslavl (case 12-70/2025). The mass media reported that during the raid, the police forced the club's visitors to lie on the floor for several hours; some people were beaten; several performers were detained, and seven administrative cases were initiated. An Uzbekistan citizen was detained for one day and ordered to leave the country for publishing a profile on a website for sex services. According to the court, on this website, this individual “carried out propaganda of non-traditional sexual relations and preferences for sex change, committed among minors.” The exact content that constituted the violation is unknown.

An individual was fined for posting a meme on VKontakte, which depicted a drawing of Quentin Tarantino with a quote attributed to him, “Making movies and not children is my motto”. In court, the defendant explained that she had uploaded the image in 2021 because she liked Tarantino and, at that time, associated the quotation with prioritising work over family rather than rejecting parenthood. On their first day, they meet Tara, the ghost of a deceased woman who now inhabits a bottle of tequila. While the girls adjust to their new surroundings, Tara acts as their mentor as they explore their bodies and sexuality. The series contains non-episodic depictions of non-traditional sexual relationships between the characters, represented by several illustrations of two female individuals in a romantic context: kissing, hugging, and sensual touching.” The court stated that “the information displayed can be classified as revealing signs of a socio-cultural threat to the national security of the Russian Federation in terms of the protection of traditional values, since it reveals signs of ideological and psychological influence on the recipient in the form of the imposition of a destructive ideology (propaganda of non-traditional sexual relations).” This is one of at least 12 cases in a serial persecution of “MangaLib”. The manager of “MangaLib” was also prosecuted at least 12 times for different publications.

В первый же день они знакомятся с Тарой -  призраком умершей женщины, обитающим ныне в бутылке с текилой. Пока девушки осваиваются на новом месте жительства, Тара занимает позицию наставницы в их знакомстве с собственным организмом и сексуальностью. Материал содержит неэпизодическое изображение нетрадиционных сексуальных отношений между персонажами, представленное несколькими иллюстрациями двух лиц женского пола в романтическом контексте: поцелуи, объятия, чувственные прикосновения.” Суд также заявил, что информация в этой публикации “может быть квалифицирована как обнаруживающая признаки социокультурной угрозы национальной безопасности РФ в части, касающейся защиты традиционных ценностей, так как обнаруживает признаки идеологического и психологического воздействия на реципиента в виде насаждения деструктивной идеологии (пропаганды нетрадиционных сексуальных отношений).” Это одно из как минимум 12 дел против “Мангалиб”. snippet_en: “New Literary Review” was fined for publishing the book by P Faxneld “Infernal Feminism” (Series “Gender Studies”) and distributing it through the bookstore “Falanster”. The judicial expert in the case concluded that the book “contains psychological and linguistic characteristics of propaganda promoting non-traditional sexual relations and a preference for sex change, as well as psychologically influencing the reader and encouraging them to engage in LGBT relationships.” According to the case, there were 55 copies available in the store that were subsequently confiscated and destroyed.

A VKontakte user was fined for posting a picture depicting “homosexual relationships between men, the content of which promotes non-traditional sexual relations”, according to the court. The exact content that constituted the violation is unknown.

An individual was fined for posts on Telegram. The exact content that constituted the violation is not mentioned. The judge stated that “the dissemination of beliefs and preferences regarding sexual orientation and specific forms of sexual relations should not infringe on the dignity of others or call into question public morality as understood in Russian society.”

An individual was fined for “promoting non-traditional sexual relations” in public by “positioning himself as a female, displaying his appearance, namely by wearing a women's shirt, women's short shorts, women's sunglasses, a red cap, lipstick, and a manicure with artificial nails painted pink.” This individual was fined twice for wearing “women's clothing” (see aslo 5-440/2025).

An individual was fined for dressing in women’s clothing in a public place. The court interpreted that as “promoting non-traditional sexual relations by appearance and behaviour. [...] while in a public place, positioned himself as a female, was dressed in women's clothing, had makeup on his face, and had manicure on his fingernails. He thereby promoted non-traditional sexual relations and committed actions aimed at fostering non-traditional sexual attitudes, the attractiveness of non-traditional sexual relations, and a distorted idea of ​​the social equivalence of traditional and non-traditional sexual relations.” This individual was fined twice for wearing “women's clothing” (see aslo 5-415/2025).

The editor-in-chief of “MOST.media” was fined for the article “You sit and think that God will punish you”. The court established that “the article, through the personal stories of its protagonists, demonstrates how people with non-traditional sexual preferences try to preserve their identity and overcome the homophobia that surrounds them.” According to the judicial expert, “the article uses verbal means of influence to form a positive attitude towards non-traditional sexual relations and (or) preferences” and its characters “are very successful and attractive individuals”, which constitutes the “promotion of non-traditional sexual relations”.
